reviews.comment: Before finding Il Forno di Napoli, delivery sourdough pizzas always arrived soggy. Their perforated thermal box kept the leopard-spotted crust crisp and the Pugliese burrata cool in the center.
Unsealing the wheat-dough purdah on the clay handi filled our entire dining room with saffron and smoked clove aroma. The meat fell off the bone effortlessly.
Separating the 18-hour tonkotsu broth from the alkaline noodles is a masterstroke. Combined at home in 30 seconds and tasted identical to eating at their chef counter.
